instruction: My roommates and I share spotify premium, which I just paid for yesterday. Request the money for it from them on venmo assuming equal share among all, with a description note, "For Spotify Premium". Skip the one/s who have already paid me for it.
notes: Roommates are discovered with phone.search_contacts(relationship=roommate); the subscription price with spotify.show_premium_subscriptions (the one paid yesterday, 2023-05-17); who already paid is discovered with venmo.show_transactions(query=spotify) by matching senders of received transactions against roommate emails. The problem instantiates a concrete scenario consistent with the 10-call reference solution: three roommates, one of whom (roommate-3) has already paid. (has-paid roommate-3) is a hidden world fact in :init (not agent knowledge); the agent is forced to discover it because venmo-create-payment-request requires (payments-checked), and the action cannot target anyone with (has-paid ?p), which encodes the skip rule. The per-person amount object amount-share is computed at runtime as price/(roommates+1); description is pinned by (note-text ...). Each request-sent fact can only be produced with the share amount and the required note, so the goal (request-sent roommate-1) (request-sent roommate-2) plus (task-completed) matches the evaluation (requests added exactly for unpaid roommates with correct amount and description, no other changes). supervisor-complete-task takes the two requested roommates as non-API parameters so its precondition mirrors the goal without quantifiers; it is the only producer of (task-completed) and every other action requires (not (task-completed)). Apps are domain constants and are not redeclared as problem objects.
